record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Under what conditions is it possible to embed a right-orderable group in a right-orderable group which has a divisible maximal locally nilpotent subgroup?

evidence.quote: 2.13∗ . Under what conditions is it possible to embed a right-orderable group in a right-orderable group which has a divisible maximal locally nilpotent subgroup?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called right-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ such that for all $a,b,c\in G$, $a\le b$ implies $ac\le bc$. A subgroup $H\le G$ is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup of $H$ is nilpotent; a maximal locally nilpotent subgroup is one that is not properly contained in any larger locally nilpotent subgroup of $G$. A group $D$ is divisible if for every $d\in D$ and every positive integer $n$ there exists $x\in D$ with $x^n=d$.

Determine conditions on a right-orderable group $G$ under which $G$ can be embedded as a subgroup into a right-orderable group $\widetilde{G}$ that possesses a maximal locally nilpotent subgroup which is divisible.
